metadata.title: Slicing a Doughnut at Random
metadata.abstract: Choose a random plane that hits a solid torus. How likely is the slice to be a single disk, and how fat should the doughnut be to make this as likely as possible? Answering requires saying precisely what a "random plane" is. We explain this from scratch, first for random lines in the plane and then for random planes in space, and then solve the problem with nothing more than calculus. Along the way we meet a two-dimensional cousin of the problem (the doughnut's shadow) and two tempting wrong turns. One wrong turn appeared in print; it turns out to be a correct solution of the two-dimensional cousin. The other was the author's own first attempt, which luckily stayed in a drawer.
